signs:
=== THE WHISPERING WOODS ===
Proceed with caution.
- The Elder Council
The old shrine lies beyond the ridge.
Rich soil here. The forest grows thick.
Safe rest stop for weary travelers.
Old boundary stones mark the village edge.

traveler.speaker: Traveling Merchant
dialogue: Ah, a traveler! These are dangerous woods.
I would offer you wares, but... I seem to have lost my cart.
If you find it, I will reward you well.

spirit.speaker: Lost Spirit
dialogue: You can see me? Most cannot...
I have wandered these woods for ages.
Seek the shrine to the east. It holds the answers you need.

wanderer.speaker: Forest Wanderer
dialogue: You're not from around here, are you?
The path ahead is treacherous. Stick to the clearings.
If you hear whispers in the wind, ignore them.

fisherman.speaker: Old Fisherman
dialogue: The water here is deep and cold.
I once saw something shimmer beneath the surface...
Best not to linger too long at the shore.

villager.speaker: Village Elder
dialogue: Welcome to our village. We don't get many visitors.
The forest has been growing thicker lately.
If you need rest, the buildings here are safe.

tree: An ancient oak. Its bark is covered in strange symbols.
A gnarled old oak. Its branches creak softly in the wind.
A tall pine. Needles sharp and dark.
A twisted elm, its roots splitting the earth.
An old birch, bark peeling in pale strips.
rock: A cluster of mossy boulders. Water trickles behind them.
Weathered stones, worn smooth by centuries of rain.
Jagged rocks jut from the dark earth.
Flat stones stacked by some forgotten hand.
A lone boulder, draped in lichen.
wall: Stone walls block your path. Old but sturdy.
Ancient masonry, cold to the touch.
Rough-hewn stone, mortar crumbling between the cracks.
A thick wall. Something scrapes from the other side.
Walls of stacked slate. Still standing after all this time.
water: Cold water ripples gently in the dim light.
The water is deep and still. No bottom in sight.
Mud and reeds line the muddy shore.
Dark water reflects nothing. It swallows all light.
A thin current tugs at the bank.
